name: yara-x
desc: Tool to do pattern matching for malware research
why: VirusTotal's Rust rewrite of YARA pattern matching, a real window into how malware signatures scan binaries.

brief.what_it_is: YARA-X is a pattern-matching tool for malware researchers, a Rust rewrite of VirusTotal's YARA. You write rules that describe a malware family or anything else, built from textual or binary patterns plus a boolean condition over them. A rule is run against files, and the output is which rules matched. The README's example rule matches any file containing one of three byte or text patterns and reports it as silent_banker. The homepage says the library has C/C++, Python and Go APIs. The brew executable is named yr, but I did not find that name or any usage in the pages I read.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the goal is to replace YARA as the default pattern matching tool for malware researchers, with a new incarnation that is faster, safer and more user-friendly than its predecessor. It also says YARA itself is still maintained, but new large features and modules will now go to YARA-X.
brief.how_it_works: Each rule has a strings section with named patterns ($a, $b, $c) written as hex byte sequences or quoted text, and a condition section that combines them with boolean operators such as or. The README says patterns can use wildcards, case-insensitive strings and regular expressions. The homepage says it is 99% rule compatible with YARA, so most existing YARA rules should run unchanged.
brief.install_notes: The fetched pages contained no install steps, no shell commands and no first-run instructions. The README mentions a Crates.io package (yara-x) and the homepage mentions APIs for C/C++, Python and Go. I did not find details on hardware, accounts or configuration. The docs page at /docs/intro/console/ returned 404, so I could not check how the yr command is used.
brief.standout: It is a drop-in-compatible rewrite of YARA, meaning most existing YARA rule sets should run unchanged, and it is the same engine VirusTotal runs in production. The README says it has been used to scan billions of files with tens of thousands of rules.
brief.status: Probably maintained. The README calls YARA-X mature and stable and says VirusTotal runs it in production. It is published on Crates.io, and the repo has CI, coverage and MSRV badges. I did not see a release date or last commit date in the pages I fetched, so the exact recency is unknown.
brief.caveats: The README gives no install instructions, so a Homebrew user has no documented first-run path from these pages. The README's rule example is YARA syntax and I did not check it against the yr binary. The README says 99% compatibility, not 100%, so a few YARA rules may behave differently; the differences are documented at /docs/writing_rules/differences-with-yara/, which I did not fetch. The licence was not visible in what I read.
quotes: The pattern matching swiss knife for malware researchers, and everyone else.
The ultimate goal of YARA-X is replacing YARA as the default pattern matching tool for malware researchers.
YARA-X is already mature and stable.

https://virustotal.github.io/yara-x/docs/intro/getting-started/ - worked, repeats the README example and points to further reading
